description.value: The study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare regional gray matter volumes between chronic cigarette smokers and matched non-smokers.

spans.text: To further investigate the effects of chronic cigarette smoking on structural brain changes, we applied whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to quantify regional gray matter volume between 44 otherwise healthy chronic cigarette smokers and 44 matched non-smoking control subjects.

design.value: A cross-sectional matched-group structural MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing 44 smokers with 44 non-smokers.

spans.text: MRI study was carried for 44 smokers and 44 matched non-smokers to assess gray matter volume differences between the two groups.
To examine differences in regional gray matter volume between groups, a voxel-wise two-sample t-test analysis in SPM5 and total gray matter volume was set as covariates.

description.value: The VBM toolbox combines tissue segmentation, bias correction and spatial normalization into a unified model. Images were multiplied (modulated) by the Jacobian determinants from the normalization step to preserve volume information. Modulated gray matter images were smoothed with a 12 mm full width at half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel for statistical analyses.

spans.text: The VBM toolbox combines tissue segmentation, bias correction and spatial normalization into a unified model. A Hidden Markov Random Field model was used to introduce spatial constraints into the segmentation process to improve accuracy of tissue segmentation. Images were multiplied (modulated) by the Jacobian determinants from the normalization step to preserve volume information. Modulated gray matter images were smoothed with a 12 mm full width at half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel for statistical analyses.
All structural data were processed with voxel-based morphometry toolbox (VBM5.1, Christian Gaser, University of Jena, Jena, Germany)
